grain_note: One table. active_opco_codes is the set of OpCos the customer was active in THAT MONTH, so: WHERE month_start_date = <month> AND opco_code = '<yours>' AND active_opco_codes @> ARRAY['<target>']. Do NOT join a second customer view. The array is PER MONTH -- overlap anywhere in a longer period is cross_opco_overlap_period.
synonyms: ["also a customer of","overlap","shared customers","how many are also","cross opco"]
description: Distinct customers of one OpCo who were also active in another, in the same month. Subject to small-cell suppression.

numerator_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_key FROM v_customer_opco_monthly WHERE month_start_date BETWEEN <from> AND <to> GROUP BY customer_key HAVING bool_or(active_opco_codes @> ARRAY['<a>']) AND bool_or(active_opco_codes @> ARRAY['<b>'])) x
grain_note: Pinned here because fact_customer_group_monthly was retired and its grain no longer enforces the distinction. active_opco_codes is a PER-MONTH set, so testing both OpCos in one predicate answers 'in the same month'. 'Anywhere in Q1' is a different, wider question and needs this grouped form -- getting it wrong silently narrows the answer rather than erroring.
synonyms: ["overlap during the quarter", "also shopped at any point", "overlap over the period", "at some point also a customer"]
description: Distinct customers active in both OpCos at ANY point in a multi-month period, not necessarily the same month.
